summary: Ray, who says he is an assassin rather than a cop, is pressed by Becker at a dinner table to explain what happened outside Ba'dai. Becker insists Ray is the lead on an investigation and points to his test scores, debriefings, and decorations. The scene turns when Becker asks Ray to reveal what really happened, and Ray says he never saw the official report, despite being the only survivor of his squad who could have written it.
one_line: Ray denies being a police investigator while Becker pushes him to reveal the truth about the Ba'dai incident in an excerpt from Book 15.
key_facts: Ray says he is not a cop and that he is not in the investigations division.
Ray describes himself as an assassin who spends much of his time trying to kill people who consider themselves outside the law.
Ray says his job is to authenticate assigned targets and carry out the hit, while finding criminals requires intelligence far beyond his share.
Becker says Ray's test scores, mission debriefings, and post-incident reports mark him as a smart guy.
Becker tells Ray that Ray has twice as many decorations as any man in the room.
Becker states that Ray is the lead on this investigation, plain and simple.
Becker asks Ray to tell him what happened outside Ba'dai, something more revelatory than the official report in Ray's service record.
Becker's official report on Ba'dai has more gaps than facts, according to the text.
Ray says he never got to see the official report on the incident.
Ray says he is the only one from his squad who made it out and the only one who could have written the report accurately.
Ray says no one ever asked him to file a report and the whole thing was made to go away.
Becker wipes his mouth with a pale linen napkin and covers his plate with it.
Ray has trouble keeping down his beer and feels no appetite while Becker eats beef.

entities.name: Ba'dai
